content.text:
Step s1 is incomplete: the project documents don't include the 10-year humidity-ageing transparency data, so no candidate can be cleared or excluded against the hard 10% constraint yet.

**What the documents contain:**
- **candidate_specs.md:** Names the three candidates only. R3 is a high-index porous radiator. R1 is a porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment. R2 is a solid radiator with a lower index. No ageing data.
- **simulation_summary_2025.md:** Separation at 10 GeV/c for a 3 cm thickness: R3 4.6σ, R1 3.8σ, R2 2.9σ. This is the only numeric performance data.
- **meeting_notes_2026-07-09.md:** Says the mirror alignment and vessel design are final. Nothing on radiators.
- **gas_volume.md:** The vessel is flushed with dry nitrogen. Nothing on ageing.
- **photodetectors.md:** MCP-PMTs with 3 mm pixels for all options. Not relevant to transparency.
- **schedule.md:** Radiator procurement starts next spring. Nothing on ageing.

**Recorded values:** The three 2025 separation figures at 3 cm. I did not record any transparency-loss values, because none exist in the documents, and I did not estimate them.

**Implication:** R1 is the one candidate with a hydrophobic treatment, which is plausibly relevant to humidity, but that is an inference, not data. R3 has the best separation on paper but is a porous radiator like R1, so it may carry the same humidity exposure risk. R2 is solid and may be less humidity-sensitive, but it has the weakest separation. None of this can be used to pass or fail a candidate against the hard constraint.

**Needed to proceed:** The 10-year-equivalent humidity-ageing transparency-loss measurement for R1, R2 and R3, ideally with the test conditions. I'd also want the thickness-dependence of transparency. I have not run any further simulations or recommended a radiator, since the separation ranking is only meaningful for candidates that pass the ageing constraint.

I could not complete the screening, so I have no eligible-radiator list to pass on. I recorded an empty results set.

What I checked:
- **Project documents:** `candidate_specs.md`, `simulation_summary_2025.md`, `meeting_notes_2026-07-09.md`, `gas_volume.md`, `schedule.md` and `photodetectors.md`.
- **Ageing data from s1:** none of these documents contains a humidity ageing test or any transparency-loss measurement. The s1 results were not passed to me, and I found no file holding them.
- **Refractive indices:** `candidate_specs.md` describes the three radiators qualitatively (R3 high-index porous, R1 porous with hydrophobic treatment, R2 solid with lower index) but gives no numeric index values.

Without the ageing data I cannot tell which radiators pass the 10% transparency-loss limit, and I did not guess. The only numbers I have are the 3 cm separations from the earlier simulation (R3 4.6σ, R1 3.8σ, R2 2.9σ), and these say nothing about ageing.

To finish this step, the s1 ageing results (transparency loss after the 10-year-equivalent humidity test for each radiator) and the refractive index values are needed. Once they are available, I can apply the 10% cut and record the eligible radiators and their indices.

I ran the pion/kaon separation sweep for all three radiators at 1–6 cm and recorded the 18 values.

| Thickness (cm) | R1 (σ) | R2 (σ) | R3 (σ) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.357 | 2.452 | 4.067 |
| 2 | 3.824 | 2.657 | 4.215 |
| 3 | 3.703 | 2.963 | 4.645 |
| 4 | 3.673 | 2.710 | 4.340 |
| 5 | 3.395 | 2.618 | 4.099 |
| 6 | 2.855 | 2.118 | 3.341 |

- **Radiator-R3** gives the best separation at every thickness, peaking at 4.645 σ at 3 cm.
- **Radiator-R1** peaks at 3.824 σ at 2 cm.
- **Radiator-R2** is lowest throughout, peaking at 2.963 σ at 3 cm.

I swept all three because none of the documents I read excluded a candidate. I did not find any humidity-ageing or transparency data in the project documents, so I could not check the 10% transparency-loss constraint. That check is needed before R3 can be recommended, and it may rule it out.

The highest separation in the recorded data is Radiator-R3 at 3 cm, with 4.645σ. I recorded this as radiator index 3, thickness 3 cm, separation 4.645σ.

**Ranking of the best thickness for each radiator:**
- R3: 4.645σ at 3 cm (next best 4.340σ at 4 cm)
- R1: 3.824σ at 2 cm
- R2: 2.963σ at 3 cm

Across all radiators and thicknesses, R3 at 3 cm is the highest. It is within the 1–6 cm range.

**The ageing constraint is not verified.** None of the project documents contain humidity-ageing or transparency data. The candidate list describes R3 as a high-index porous radiator and R1 as a porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment. R1 is the only option whose description mentions humidity protection. The ageing requirement is a hard constraint and the radiator cannot be replaced, so R3 at 3 cm should not be submitted as final until its 10-year humidity transparency loss is confirmed at or below 10%. If R3 fails that test, the best eligible option is R1 at 2 cm (3.824σ), which also needs its ageing result confirmed.

content.text:
**Recommendation (conditional): Radiator-R3 at 3 cm, pion/kaon separation 4.645σ at 10 GeV/c.**

I could not confirm the transparency-ageing constraint, so this recommendation should not be treated as final yet.

- **Separation:** R3 at 3 cm gives the best value in the scan (4.645σ). It is the best of all thicknesses and radiators tested, ahead of R1 at 2 cm (3.82σ) and R2 at 3 cm (2.96σ). The 2025 summary also gives R3 at 4.6σ, which agrees.
- **Transparency after 10-year humidity ageing:** Not verified. The project documents contain no ageing or transparency data for any candidate. The simulation tool only returns separation, so I have no measured value to check against the 10% hard limit.
- **Risk:** R3 is described as a high-index porous radiator with no humidity treatment. R1 is a porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment, which suggests better humidity tolerance. That makes R3's ageing result the main open question. If R3 fails the 10% limit, R1 is the fallback. Its best scanned option is 2 cm at 3.82σ.
- **Recorded:** final radiator index 3, thickness 3 cm, separation 4.645σ. I did not record an ageing value because none exists in the data.

**Next step before procurement:** run a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test on R3 at 3 cm, and on R1 at 2 cm as a fallback. Radiator procurement starts next spring, so there is time to do this.

input.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm gives the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c among the candidates and thicknesses tested: 4.645 sigma from the thickness scan, versus a best of 3.824 for R1 (at 2 cm) and 2.963 for R2 (at 3 cm). R3 is the best option at every thickness from 1 to 6 cm, and 3 cm is its peak. The simulation summary gives 4.6 sigma for R3 at 3 cm, 3.8 for R1 and 2.9 for R2, which agrees with the scan for R3 and R2 but is about 0.1 sigma higher than the scan for R1 (3.703 at 3 cm). The ranking is unchanged either way. However, the hard transparency constraint is NOT verified. The recorded results contain no 10-year humidity-ageing transparency measurement for any candidate, and candidate_specs.md was not among the results I was given. This recommendation is therefore conditional: the transparency loss of R3 after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing must be confirmed to be at most 10% before the radiator is committed, because it cannot be replaced during the run. If R3 fails that check, the choice must be revisited; I cannot certify it from the available data.
